task.title: Sign embed tokens in your backend
task.shortdesc: Your app already knows who is signed in. Its backend proves that to with a short-lived token signed with a shared secret.

prereq.p: You need the deployment's embed secret, OPEND_EMBED_SECRET, in your backend's configuration. Treat it like a password: anyone holding it can sign in as any registered reader. Never send it to the browser.

context.p: The token only says who the user is. What they may read still comes from : their organization's entitlements. A host app therefore cannot grant more than allows.

step.cmd: Add an endpoint that returns a token for the signed-in user.

stepxmp.p: Or with nothing but Node's crypto module:

step.cmd: Return it from the widget's getToken.

strow.stentry: HS256 with OPEND_EMBED_SECRET. Other algorithms are refused.
The docs site's PUBLIC_URL, exactly, without a trailing slash.
Both required. The lifetime, exp minus iat, must be at most 600 seconds. 30 seconds of clock skew are tolerated.
The reader's email as registered in . A sub holding an email is accepted instead.
The slug of the reader's organization. It must match the organization registered for that email.

result.p: An invalid or expired token gets 401. A valid token for an email that is not registered, or for the wrong organization, gets 403. A good token is exchanged for an opend_embed session cookie that lasts 60 minutes, after which the panel asks for a new token.
